He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] and was selected 42nd overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He has also played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Toronto Raptors]], and [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. In [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]], he was a key contributor of the Nuggets' championship run off the bench. Despite being undersized, Brown plays the [[small forward]] and both [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] positions. ==High school career== Brown played basketball and [[American football|football]] for [[Wakefield Memorial High School]] in [[Wakefield, Massachusetts]]. For his junior season, he transferred to [[Vermont Academy]] in [[Saxtons River, Vermont]].{{cite web |title=Bruce Brown, Jr. |date=June 2, 2017 |url=https://hurricanesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/bruce-brown-jr-/4379 |access-date=May 21, 2020 |publisher=University of Miami Athletics}} As a senior, Brown led his team to the [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] Class AA title and was named tournament [[most valuable player]].{{cite web |last=White |first=Josh |title=Bruce Brown's all-around game having huge impact on Miami early in the season |url=https://www.themiamihurricane.com/2016/12/16/bruce-brown-profile/ |website=[[The Miami Hurricane]] |access-date=May 21, 2020 |date=December 16, 2016}} He was selected to play in the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web |title=Bruce Brown just wants to compete when it comes to Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/bruce-brown-just-wants-to-compete-when-it-comes-to-jordan-brand-classic |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 21, 2020 |date=April 4, 2016}} Brown was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] and [[ESPN]] and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. Brown was ranked no. 26 overall recruit and fifth-best shooting guard in the 2016 high school class.{{Cite web |date=April 26, 2016 |title=Bruce Brown – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/165875 |access-date=April 26, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web |date=May 14, 2016 |title=Bruce Brown, 2016 Shooting guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/bruce-brown-468 |access-date=May 14, 2016 |website=Rivals.com}} On November 18, 2015, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] over an offer from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], among others.{{cite magazine |last=Johnson |first=Chris |title=What Bruce Brown's commitment means for Miami Hurricanes |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/11/18/bruce-brown-recruiting-commits-miami-hurricanes |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 21, 2020 |date=November 18, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:Bruce Brown Miami (cropped2).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Brown with the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] in 2017]] As a sophomore with the Miami Hurricanes, Brown averaged 11.4 points, 7.1 rebounds and four assists per game and shot 27 percent from three-point range.{{cite news|last=McMillen|first=Gabrielle|title=Miami G Bruce Brown Jr. undergoing surgery on left foot|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/miami-hurricanes-guard-bruce-brown-surgery-left-foot-timeline-out-six-weeks/qfg8ceyayrfr1b1vlijonybwz|access-date=April 2, 2018|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=January 30, 2018|archive-date=July 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709010133/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/miami-hurricanes-guard-bruce-brown-surgery-left-foot-timeline-out-six-weeks/qfg8ceyayrfr1b1vlijonybwz|url-status=dead}} He only played 19 games and missed the postseason with a left foot injury that required surgery. After the season Brown declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent, thereby allowing for the possibility of returning to college.{{cite news|title=Miami Hurricanes' Bruce Brown Jr. will test NBA Draft waters|url=https://www.foxsports.com/florida/story/miami-hurricanes-bruce-brown-jr-will-test-nba-draft-waters-032218|access-date=April 2, 2018|work=Fox Sports|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 22, 2018}} He ultimately decided to stay in the draft.{{cite news |date=May 26, 2018 |title=Hurricanes' Dewan Huell opts out of NBA draft, returning for junior season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23614173 |access-date=November 26, 2024 |work=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} {{clear left}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2018–2020)=== On June 21, 2018, Brown was drafted 42nd overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite news|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2018/06/21/detroit-pistons-2018-nba-draft/720696002/ |title=Detroit Pistons get Khyri Thomas in trade with 76ers, add Bruce Brown |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Marlowe |last=Alter |date=June 21, 2018 |access-date=June 22, 2018}}{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2018/06/21/pistons-take-miamis-bruce-brown/36267219/ |title=Pistons draft Miami's Brown, trade for Creighton's Thomas |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=June 21, 2018 |access-date=June 22, 2018}} He made his NBA debut on October 17, 2018, against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], scoring no points with two rebounds and an assist in 19 minutes of action.{{cite web|url=https://caneswarning.com/2018/10/17/miami-basketball-alum-bruce-brown-starts-scoreless-nba-debut/|title=Miami basketball alum Bruce Brown starts but is scoreless in NBA Debut|first=Alan|last=Rubenstein|work=CanesWarning.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018|archive-date=December 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191202220232/https://caneswarning.com/2018/10/17/miami-basketball-alum-bruce-brown-starts-scoreless-nba-debut/|url-status=dead}} On November 2, 2019, he posted 22 points and seven assists, with no turnovers, in a 113–109 win over the Nets.{{cite web |last=Ellis |first=Vince |title=Detroit Pistons mailbag: Will Reggie Jackson be around by season's end? |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2019/11/04/detroit-pistons-bruce-brown-point-guard-reggie-jackson/4139481002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=May 21, 2020 |date=November 4, 2019}} On February 2, 2020, Brown recorded 19 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists in a 128–123 overtime victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |title=Pistons' Bruce Brown: Flirts with triple-double |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-bruce-brown-flirts-with-triple-double/ |work=CBS Sports |access-date=May 21, 2020 |date=February 3, 2020}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2020–2022)=== On November 19, 2020, Brown was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Landry Shamet, Bruce Brown and the Draft Rights to Reggie Perry in Three-team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/11/19/brooklyn-nets-acquire-landry-shamet-bruce-brown-and-draft-rights-reggie-perry-three-team-trade |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 20, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}} On February 23, 2021, Brown scored a career-high 29 points in the Nets' 127–118 win against the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last=Dowd |first=Tom |title=Nets 127, Kings 118: Bruce Brown Scores Career-High 29 Points to Lead Brooklyn |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/recap/2021/02/23/nets-127-kings-118-bruce-brown-scores-career-high-29-points-to-lead-brooklyn |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 24, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} On April 23, 2022, he scored a team leading 26 points for the Nets in a losing effort against the Celtics in the first round of the NBA playoffs. The Nets fell to 0–3 after that game.{{Cite web |title=2022 NBA Eastern Conference First Round Game 3: Celtics vs Nets, April 23, 2022 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202204230BRK.html |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} His performance in games 2 and 3 were notably impressive, as he scored 23 or more points in both contests, despite eclipsing 20 points only four times throughout the entire regular season. ===Denver Nuggets (2022–2023)=== On July 7, 2022, Brown signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-bruce-brown|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Bruce Brown|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2022}} He signed a two-year contract worth $13 million, with a player option on the second year.{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Jordanna |date=June 4, 2023 |title=Bruce Brown-Nets storyline more than enough to amuse Knicks fans |url=https://dailyknicks.com/2023/06/04/bruce-brown-nets-storyline-enough-amuse-knicks-fans/ |access-date=November 26, 2024 |website=DailyKnicks.com}} The Nets had chosen not to match the Nuggets' [[NBA salary cap|taxpayer mid-level exception]] offer for Brown and acquired [[Royce O'Neale]] as a replacement instead.{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Brian |date=2022-07-02 |title=Nets lose Bruce Brown, Andre Drummond in free agency |url=https://nypost.com/2022/07/02/nets-lose-bruce-brown-andre-drummond-in-free-agency/ |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=nypost.com |language=en-US}} On November 23, Brown recorded a [[triple double|triple-double]] with 17 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists during a win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2022 |title=Nuggets' Bruce Brown: Triple-doubles in OT victory |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-bruce-brown-triple-doubles-in-ot-victory/ |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} In 2023, Brown and the Nuggets reached the [[2023 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where they defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in five games to give Brown his first [[NBA championship]].{{cite web |last=Benedetto |first=Vinny |date=May 27, 2023 |title=Bruce Brown focused on NBA Finals run with Nuggets rather than busy offseason |url=https://denvergazette.com/sports/denver-nuggets/bruce-brown-focused-on-nba-finals-run-with-nuggets-rather-than-busy-offseason/article_fa98bfbc-fc22-11ed-83b0-4347b27786bc.html |access-date=November 26, 2024 |website=DenverGazette.com}} In game 4 of the series, Brown scored a pivotal 21 points, including 11 in the fourth quarter, to help Denver open up a 3–1 series lead with a 108–95 victory over the Heat.{{cite web |last=Koons |first=Zach |date=June 9, 2023 |title=Bruce Brown's Fourth-Quarter Explosion in Game 4 Left NBA World in Awe |url=https://www.si.com/.amp/extra-mustard/2023/06/10/bruce-brown-fourth-quarter-explosion-game-4-nba-fans-in-awe |access-date=November 26, 2024 |website=SportsIllustrated.com}} In Game 5, Brown scored the winning points on a layup off an offensive rebound with just over 90 seconds left in the game, and hit two free throws to make it a two-possession game with less than 30 seconds remaining as the Nuggets defeated Miami 94–89 to win their first championship in franchise history after a 47-year drought. ===Indiana Pacers (2023–2024)=== On July 6, 2023, Brown signed a two-year, $45 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=NBA champ Bruce Brown signs with Pacers|url=https://www.nba.com/news/bruce-brown-2023-free-agency|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} He saw an increased role in Indiana, earning a starting position as the highest-paid Pacer for the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|2023–24 season]]. On October 25, Brown impressed in his Pacers debut, scoring a team-high 24 points with a career-high 6-of-8 three-point shooting performance, along with three rebounds and a steal in a 143–120 win over the [[2023–24 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|first=Chloe|last=Peterson|title='Naked under the overalls?': After cowboy attire debut, Bruce Brown impresses for Pacers|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2023/10/26/pacers-after-cowboy-debut-bruce-brown-impresses-for-indiana/71284268007/|website=IndyStar.com|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}} He started 33 contests for Indiana, recording averages of 12.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 3.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=Bruce Brown 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065670/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2025)=== On January 17, 2024, the Pacers traded Brown, along with [[Jordan Nwora]], [[Kira Lewis Jr.]] and three first-round draft picks to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Pascal Siakam]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH INDIANA|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-indiana-2|website=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 18, 2024}} He made 34 appearances (including 11 starts) for Toronto during the remainder of the year, averaging 9.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 2.7 assists. Brown played in 18 contests for the Raptors in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 8.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Bruce Brown 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4065670/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2025)=== On February 6, 2025, the Raptors traded Brown, [[Kelly Olynyk]] and multiple draft picks to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Brandon Ingram]].{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans complete trade with Toronto Raptors|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-trade-toronto-raptors-nba-trade-deadline-brandon-ingram-february-6-2025|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} In 23 appearances (including 12 starts) for New Orleans, Brown posted averages of 8.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 2.4 assists. === Return to Denver (2025–2026) === On July 9, 2025, Brown signed a one-year contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{Cite web |title=NUGGETS SIGN BRUCE BROWN {{!}} Denver Nuggets |url=https://nuggets.com/news/nuggets-sign-bruce-brown |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=nuggets.com |language=en}} Brown appeared in all 82 games (including four starts) for the Nuggets during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 7.9 points, 3.9 points, and 2.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men.
